newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 2.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Wednesday that domestic economic problems are not rooted primarily in the foreign trade deficit, but in slowing economic growth rate. Dlouhy's ministry supports efforts for entry into the Asian Development Bank, which could contribute in the long term to pushing Czech goods in southeast Asia.
- According to the cabinet's decision, 43.3 percent of glass maker Moser a.s. will go by direct sale to Iris s.r.o. This will increase Iris's stake to 68.3 percent.
- The strike of about 200 doctors and nurses from Motol Hospital will continue today, and students of the Second Medical Faculty of Charles University should join in.

- During celebrations for May 1 yesterday, the head of the opposition Social Democrats, Milos Zeman, criticised the strongest coalition party. The chairman of the Communist Party, Miroslav Grebenicek, urged a mass protest against the cabinet's "impoverishing policy".
- The Czech Republic's yearly contribution to NATO could amount to from 1.6 to two billion crowns.
- The cabinet must approve the contract between Aero Vodochody and the Czech Army for 72 subsonic L-159 fighter aircraft before it can be signed.
- Gramofonove Zavody, one of the largest independent manufacturers of CDs and records in Europe, had sales of 937 million crowns last year, an increase of 20 percent over 1995.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The European Commission's disagreement with the new import deposit system in the Czech Republic does not mean, according to experts, that the measure will be called off. The Czech cabinet will present detailed information to the EU in the next few weeks which should convince the commission that the measure is necessary.

- From May 5, Komercni Banka will change its interest rates; for time deposits they should increase slightly and decrease for other kinds of deposits. The bank's reference rate will decrease to 12.05 percent from 12.25 percent.
- SPT Telecom had profits of 1.59 billion crowns for the first quarter of this year, 9.5 percent less than at the same time last year.

- Japanese Nomura bank, which is one of the candidates in the tender for IPB bank, already indirectly owns a stake in the bank. According to the latest reports from the Security Centre, one of the largest shareholders of IPB is Nutshell, whose agent is the director of Nomura's Czech representation, Eduard Onderka.
PRAVO - The general director and chairman of the board of bank IPB and his deputy and board member were taken to jail on Wednesday. They are charged with fraud and breaking rules of economic conduct.

- The cabinet supports the intentions of the Czech-Moravian Football League to support the European championship in 2004 together with Austria and will give a grant of 1.5 billion crowns to the league this year.

- During the first quarter of this year, Komercni Banka had profits after taxes of 1.04 billion crowns according to international accounting standards. Its balance sum was 443.9 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of 11 percent.

- Assembly of Skoda Octavias in the Polish Volkswagen factory should begin in September of this year. Production of Skoda cars in the Polish factory should increase to 30,000 this year from 16,000 last year.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After the cabinet's meeting on Wednesday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and Education Minister Ivan Pilip distanced themselves from the apparent intention to cancel General Facutly Hospital in Prague.
- The Czech branch of Interpol will probably have Vratislav Gregr as new director to replace Frantisek Zelenicky.
- After nearly two years of preparations, the Central Energy Dispatcher (UED) began operating yesterday. The cabinet will decide on UED's concrete operations on June 12.
- Pragobanka, part of Ceska Pojistovna Group, signed a contract with the central bank to enter its stabilisation programme.
- Yesterday morning, the first Norwegian natural gas crossed the Czech border, ending the country's dependence on Russia for this commodity.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
